reviews.t: Very cool architecture, calming spot in the world. Seems to be a very clean, quiet, & welcoming space.
Beautiful church with wonderful people and very kind pastor. Thank you Mr. Steve Runholt for giving me an opportunity to visit the church and see the Sunday worship.

Warren Wilson Presbyterian Church members are friendly and enthusiastic about supporting their community and church home. Pastor Margaret's sermons are always interesting and thought-provoking. The service music program is a joy! My husband and I found this church when we moved to Swannanoa a few years ago. We have made wonderful, dear friends there and engaged in many worthwhile community service activities supported by the church. This church has truly helped us become part of the Swannanoa community.

Took us a long time to find our church home when we first moved here, but this one made the whole search well worth it! Wonderful community of open-minded, inspiring folks who strive hard to embody the love that Christ taught us to show to one another. Before this church, I never thought it was possible to find a worship space that touched my soul on every level. I had craved a welcoming, progressive congregation with provoking sermons and a traditional worship style - that was rich with the hymns I recall hearing as a child. I recommend taking a moment to step inside this beautiful chapel and see if the sound of the organ doesn't fill your heart up too.

As someone who is queer and on the autism spectrum, finding a place to worship that feels non-judgemental, welcoming, and safe has been a journey. The last 7 months at WWPC have been wonderful. The people are welcoming, open minded, and accepting. Margaret incorporated autism into her sermon today and invited me to speak to the adult study group about how we, as a church, can be more inclusive of folks on the spectrum. There are a few of us on the spectrum at church and accommodations have been made for us without anyone requesting it. For instance, there's a safe sensory cubby in the main hall. I've never been to a church that offers anything like this before. It can be hard to heal the trauma that religion and church has brought many of us who are different during our growing up years. If you're ready to let the past go and connect to a sense of Belonging, Community, and the Divine, come join us Sunday morning at 11. You'll be made welcome regardless of race, gender identity, neurotype, past religious experiences, etc. No one will attempt to "recruit you" and there's no cost for the service. Come feel it out. Maybe you could find a new place where you feel like you Belong, the way that I did.

This is a very welcoming place and the people are so engaging. The serivce is relaxed, but orderly and inspiring. Great music and varied sermon topics along with many opportunities for after service fellowship. The facilities are a true inspiration as well. A wonderful place for nature and nurture. A true jewel in the WNC mountains.

A warm and very natural sanctuary, a welcoming congregation from seniors to toddlers, and a thoughtful and caring staff. This is a comfortable place to worship and interact with a nice variety of people.

this is sister's/brother-in-law's beloved church.. I can honestly say WWC Presby has ALWAYS been such a lovely place with wonderful, caring congregation. ☆ I truly MISS 💜 Dr Steven Williams, former MD (rihp)💜.. however, Joel, new MD, is great. …

A warm, welcoming community of seeking human beings, struggling with all the usual things life has to offer, being supported by their faith and one another, growing outwardly and inwardly, actively seeking to open minds and hearts as taught by Christ and led by the Spirit.
Beautiful, peaceful campus. Loved this thoughtful banner on the chapel’s door.
